  1100→+<span class="key">GET</span> <span class="str">/json/countries</span>    <span class="cm">-- all countries with counts</span>
  1101→+<span class="key">GET</span> <span class="str">/json/languages</span>   <span class="cm">-- all languages with counts</span>
  1102→+<span class="key">GET</span> <span class="str">/json/codecs</span>      <span class="cm">-- all codecs with counts</span></code></pre>
  1103→+
  1104→+  <h4>Get Resolved Stream URL</h4>
  1105→+  <pre><code><span class="key">GET</span> <span class="str">/json/url/{stationuuid}</span>
  1106→+
  1107→+<span class="cm">Returns:</span>
  1108→+{
  1109→+  <span class="key">"url"</span>: <span class="str">"https://original.url/stream"</span>,
  1110→+  <span class="key">"url_resolved"</span>: <span class="str">"https://actual.server/stream.mp3"</span>,  <span class="cm">// direct stream</span>
  1111→+  <span class="key">"stationuuid"</span>: <span class="str">"abc-123-def"</span>
  1112→+}
  1113→+<span class="cm">// Also increments the station's click counter</span></code></pre>
  1114→+
  1115→+  <h3>Station Object</h3>
  1116→+  <pre><code>{
  1117→+  <span class="key">"stationuuid"</span>: <span class="str">"abc-123"</span>,
  1118→+  <span class="key">"name"</span>: <span class="str">"Underground FM"</span>,
  1119→+  <span class="key">"url"</span>: <span class="str">"https://stream.example.com/radio"</span>,
  1120→+  <span class="key">"url_resolved"</span>: <span class="str">"https://..."</span>,
  1121→+  <span class="key">"homepage"</span>: <span class="str">"https://..."</span>,
  1122→+  <span class="key">"favicon"</span>: <span class="str">"https://..."</span>,
  1123→+  <span class="key">"tags"</span>: <span class="str">"electronic,underground,pirate"</span>,
  1124→+  <span class="key">"country"</span>: <span class="str">"United States"</span>,
  1125→+  <span class="key">"countrycode"</span>: <span class="str">"US"</span>,
  1126→+  <span class="key">"language"</span>: <span class="str">"english"</span>,
  1127→+  <span class="key">"codec"</span>: <span class="str">"MP3"</span>,
  1128→+  <span class="key">"bitrate"</span>: <span class="num">128</span>,
  1129→+  <span class="key">"votes"</span>: <span class="num">42</span>,
  1130→+  <span class="key">"clickcount"</span>: <span class="num">1337</span>,
  1131→+  <span class="key">"lastcheckok"</span>: <span class="num">1</span>,           <span class="cm">// 1 = online, 0 = broken</span>
  1132→+  <span class="key">"hls"</span>: <span class="num">0</span>,
  1133→+  <span class="key">"geo_lat"</span>: <span class="num">37.7749</span>,
  1134→+  <span class="key">"geo_long"</span>: <span class="num">-122.4194</span>
  1135→+}</code></pre>
  1136→+
  1137→+  <div class="callout">
  1138→+    <strong>Usage Notes:</strong> Set a descriptive <code>User-Agent</code> header. Use <code>url_resolved</code> for direct playback (bypasses playlist file parsing). Click counting is limited to once per IP per station per day. All GET params can be sent as POST with JSON body.
  1139→+  </div>
  1140→+
  1141→+  <h3>Useful Tag Searches for Pirate Radio</h3>
  1142→+  <pre><code><span class="cm">// Underground/pirate-adjacent tags:</span>
  1143→+<span class="str">"pirate"</span>, <span class="str">"underground"</span>, <span class="str">"independent"</span>, <span class="str">"college"</span>, <span class="str">"community"</span>,
  1144→+<span class="str">"freeform"</span>, <span class="str">"experimental"</span>, <span class="str">"lo-fi"</span>, <span class="str">"punk"</span>, <span class="str">"diy"</span>,
  1145→+<span class="str">"noise"</span>, <span class="str">"avant-garde"</span>, <span class="str">"alternative"</span>, <span class="str">"anarchist"</span></code></pre>
  1146→+</section>
  1147→+
  1148→+<!-- =============== ICECAST =============== -->
  1149→+<section id="icecast">
  1150→+  <h2>4. Icecast Directory (dir.xiph.org)</h2>
  1151→+
  1152→+  <p>The Xiph.org Icecast directory provides a machine-readable XML feed of Icecast-registered stations. Smaller than Radio Browser but contains stations that may not appear elsewhere, particularly hobbyist and underground broadcasters.</p>
  1153→+
  1154→+  <h3>Endpoint</h3>
  1155→+  <pre><code><span class="key">GET</span> <span class="str">https://dir.xiph.org/yp.xml</span></code></pre>
  1156→+
  1157→+  <h3>Entry Structure</h3>
  1158→+  <pre><code><span class="kw">&lt;entry&gt;</span>
  1159→+  <span class="key">&lt;server_name&gt;</span>Underground Radio<span class="key">&lt;/server_name&gt;</span>
  1160→+  <span class="key">&lt;server_type&gt;</span>audio/mpeg<span class="key">&lt;/server_type&gt;</span>
  1161→+  <span class="key">&lt;bitrate&gt;</span>128<span class="key">&lt;/bitrate&gt;</span>
  1162→+  <span class="key">&lt;samplerate&gt;</span>44100<span class="key">&lt;/samplerate&gt;</span>
  1163→+  <span class="key">&lt;channels&gt;</span>2<span class="key">&lt;/channels&gt;</span>
  1164→+  <span class="key">&lt;listen_url&gt;</span>https://stream.example.com/radio<span class="key">&lt;/listen_url&gt;</span>
  1165→+  <span class="key">&lt;current_song&gt;</span>Artist - Track<span class="key">&lt;/current_song&gt;</span>
  1166→+  <span class="key">&lt;genre&gt;</span>electronic experimental<span class="key">&lt;/genre&gt;</span>
  1167→+<span class="kw">&lt;/entry&gt;</span></code></pre>
  1168→+
  1169→+  <p>Audio formats include <code>audio/mpeg</code> (MP3), <code>audio/aac</code>, <code>audio/aacp</code>, <code>application/ogg</code>, and <code>audio/mp4</code>. Bitrates range from 16 kbps (talk/scanner) to 1024 kbps (high-fidelity music). The <code>listen_url</code> values are direct stream URLs -- no playlist resolution needed.</p>
  1170→+
  1171→+  <div class="callout warn">
  1172→+    <strong>Limitation:</strong> The Icecast directory is a flat XML file with no search/filter API. You must fetch the entire file and filter client-side. Best treated as a supplementary source parsed on startup and cached.
  1173→+  </div>
  1174→+</section>
  1175→+
  1176→+<hr>
  1177→+
  1178→+<!-- =============== TTS =============== -->
  1179→+<section id="tts">
  1180→+  <h2>5. TTS for Mic Breaks</h2>
  1181→+
  1182→+  <p>For creating radio DJ-style announcements between songs or during station changes. The key requirement is generating natural-sounding speech, saving it to a file (or buffer), and inserting it into the audio playback stream.</p>
  1183→+
  1184→+  <h3>Option Comparison</h3>
  1185→+
  1186→+  <div class="table-wrap">
  1187→+    <table>
  1188→+      <thead><tr><th>Solution</th><th>Quality</th><th>Cost</th><th>Latency</th><th>Offline</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
  1189→+      <tbody>
  1190→+        <tr>
  1191→+          <td><strong>Edge TTS</strong></td>
  1192→+          <td>High (neural)</td>
  1193→+          <td>Free</td>
  1194→+          <td>~1-2s</td>
  1195→+          <td>No</td>
  1196→+          <td><span class="badge badge-rec">RECOMMENDED</span></td>
  1197→+        </tr>
  1198→+        <tr>
  1199→+          <td><strong>ElevenLabs</strong></td>
  1200→+          <td>Excellent</td>
  1201→+          <td>$5+/mo</td>
  1202→+          <td>~2-4s</td>
  1203→+          <td>No</td>
  1204→+          <td><span class="badge badge-wip">PREMIUM</span></td>
  1205→+        </tr>
  1206→+        <tr>
  1207→+          <td><strong>Piper TTS</strong></td>
  1208→+          <td>Good</td>
  1209→+          <td>Free</td>
  1210→+          <td>~0.5s</td>
  1211→+          <td>Yes</td>
  1212→+          <td><span class="badge badge-done">FALLBACK</span></td>
  1213→+        </tr>
  1214→+        <tr>
  1215→+          <td><strong>say.js</strong></td>
  1216→+          <td>Low-Med</td>
  1217→+          <td>Free</td>
  1218→+          <td>~0.2s</td>
  1219→+          <td>Yes</td>
  1220→+          <td><span class="badge badge-todo">BASIC</span></td>
  1221→+        </tr>
  1222→+      </tbody>
  1223→+    </table>
  1224→+  </div>
  1225→+
  1226→+  <h3>Edge TTS (Recommended Default)</h3>
  1227→+
  1228→+  <p>Uses Microsoft Edge's online neural TTS service. No API key needed, no account required, high-quality neural voices, 400+ voices across 100+ languages. Free with no documented rate limits (uses the same endpoint as Edge browser's Read Aloud feature).</p>
  1229→+
  1230→+  <h4>Best Node.js Packages</h4>
  1231→+  <div class="table-wrap">
  1232→+    <table>
  1233→+      <thead><tr><th>Package</th><th>Version</th><th>Last Updated</th><th>License</th><th>Notes</th></tr></thead>
  1234→+      <tbody>
  1235→+        <tr>
  1236→+          <td><code>@andresaya/edge-tts</code></td>
  1237→+          <td>1.8.0</td>
  1238→+          <td>2025-12</td>
  1239→+          <td>GPL-3.0</td>
  1240→+          <td>Most complete API, streaming, word boundaries, 36+ output formats</td>
  1241→+        </tr>
  1242→+        <tr>
  1243→+          <td><code>@bestcodes/edge-tts</code></td>
  1244→+          <td>3.0.1</td>
  1245→+          <td>2025-12</td>
  1246→+          <td>MIT</td>
  1247→+          <td>Clean API, streaming, &lt;50kb bundle, MIT license</td>
  1248→+        </tr>
  1249→+        <tr>
  1250→+          <td><code>node-edge-tts</code></td>
  1251→+          <td>1.2.10</td>
  1252→+          <td>2026-02</td>
  1253→+          <td>MIT</td>
  1254→+          <td>Actively maintained, simple promise API, subtitle support</td>
  1255→+        </tr>
  1256→+      </tbody>
  1257→+    </table>
  1258→+  </div>
  1259→+
  1260→+  <h4>Usage with @bestcodes/edge-tts</h4>
  1261→+  <pre><code><span class="kw">import</span> { EdgeTTS } <span class="kw">from</span> <span class="str">'@bestcodes/edge-tts'</span>;
  1262→+
  1263→+<span class="kw">const</span> tts = <span class="kw">new</span> EdgeTTS();
  1264→+
  1265→+<span class="cm">// Generate to buffer</span>
  1266→+<span class="kw">const</span> audio = <span class="kw">await</span> tts.generateSpeech({
  1267→+  text: <span class="str">"You're locked in to Underground FM, broadcasting from the edge of nowhere."</span>,
  1268→+  voice: <span class="str">"en-US-GuyNeural"</span>,       <span class="cm">// male, natural</span>
  1269→+  rate: <span class="str">"-5%"</span>,                     <span class="cm">// slightly slower for DJ vibe</span>
  1270→+  pitch: <span class="str">"-2Hz"</span>,                   <span class="cm">// slightly lower pitch</span>
  1271→+});
  1272→+
  1273→+<span class="cm">// Or generate to file</span>
  1274→+<span class="kw">await</span> tts.generateSpeechToFile({
  1275→+  text: <span class="str">"Next up, we've got something special..."</span>,
  1276→+  voice: <span class="str">"en-US-AndrewNeural"</span>,
  1277→+  outputPath: <span class="str">"/tmp/mic-break.mp3"</span>,
  1278→+});
  1279→+
  1280→+<span class="cm">// Stream chunks for real-time playback</span>
  1281→+<span class="kw">for await</span> (<span class="kw">const</span> chunk <span class="kw">of</span> tts.streamSpeech({ text, voice })) {
  1282→+  <span class="cm">// pipe to audio output</span>
  1283→+}</code></pre>
  1284→+
  1285→+  <h4>Usage with @andresaya/edge-tts</h4>
  1286→+  <pre><code><span class="kw">import</span> { EdgeTTS } <span class="kw">from</span> <span class="str">'@andresaya/edge-tts'</span>;
  1287→+
  1288→+<span class="kw">const</span> tts = <span class="kw">new</span> EdgeTTS();
  1289→+
  1290→+<span class="cm">// Synthesize with full control</span>
  1291→+<span class="kw">await</span> tts.synthesize(
  1292→+  <span class="str">"You're tuned in to the frequency. Don't touch that dial."</span>,
  1293→+  <span class="str">'en-US-DavisNeural'</span>,
  1294→+  { rate: <span class="str">'-10%'</span>, volume: <span class="str">'+20%'</span>, pitch: <span class="str">'-5Hz'</span> }
  1295→+);
  1296→+
  1297→+<span class="cm">// Export</span>
  1298→+<span class="kw">await</span> tts.toFile(<span class="str">"mic-break"</span>);        <span class="cm">// auto-detects extension</span>
  1299→+<span class="kw">const</span> buffer = tts.toBuffer();          <span class="cm">// get Buffer directly</span>
  1300→+<span class="kw">const</span> duration = tts.getDuration();     <span class="cm">// seconds</span>
  1301→+
  1302→+<span class="cm">// 36+ output formats available:</span>
  1303→+<span class="cm">// MP3 (16/24/48kHz), Opus, WebM, OGG, WAV/PCM, AMR-WB, G.722, TrueSilk</span></code></pre>
  1304→+
  1305→+  <h4>Good DJ Voices (Edge TTS)</h4>
  1306→+  <ul>
  1307→+    <li><code>en-US-GuyNeural</code> -- deep male, warm radio tone</li>
  1308→+    <li><code>en-US-DavisNeural</code> -- confident male</li>
  1309→+    <li><code>en-US-AndrewNeural</code> -- natural male</li>
  1310→+    <li><code>en-US-AriaNeural</code> -- clear female</li>
  1311→+    <li><code>en-US-JennyNeural</code> -- friendly female</li>
  1312→+    <li><code>en-GB-RyanNeural</code> -- British male, good for pirate radio persona</li>
  1313→+    <li><code>en-AU-WilliamNeural</code> -- Australian male</li>
  1314→+  </ul>
  1315→+
  1316→+  <h3>ElevenLabs (Premium Option)</h3>
  1317→+
  1318→+  <p>State-of-the-art voice synthesis. Most natural-sounding option by far. Has voice cloning for creating a unique DJ persona. Costs money but quality is unmatched.</p>
  1319→+
  1320→+  <pre><code><span class="key">POST</span> <span class="str">https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}</span>
  1321→+
  1322→+<span class="cm">Headers:</span>
  1323→+  <span class="key">xi-api-key</span>: <span class="str">your-api-key</span>
  1324→+  <span class="key">Content-Type</span>: <span class="str">application/json</span>
  1325→+
  1326→+<span class="cm">Body:</span>
  1327→+{
  1328→+  <span class="key">"text"</span>: <span class="str">"You're listening to the signal."</span>,
  1329→+  <span class="key">"model_id"</span>: <span class="str">"eleven_multilingual_v2"</span>,
  1330→+  <span class="key">"voice_settings"</span>: {
  1331→+    <span class="key">"stability"</span>: <span class="num">0.5</span>,
  1332→+    <span class="key">"similarity_boost"</span>: <span class="num">0.8</span>,
  1333→+    <span class="key">"style"</span>: <span class="num">0.3</span>,
  1334→+    <span class="key">"speed"</span>: <span class="num">0.9</span>
  1335→+  }
  1336→+}
  1337→+
  1338→+<span class="cm">Output formats: mp3_44100_128 (default), pcm_44100, wav_44100, opus_48000_128</span>
  1339→+<span class="cm">Response: binary audio stream (application/octet-stream)</span></code></pre>
  1340→+
  1341→+  <div class="callout">
  1342→+    <strong>Pricing:</strong> Free tier gives ~10k characters/month. Starter is $5/month for 30k chars. For occasional mic breaks (short phrases every few minutes), the free tier might suffice. Voice cloning requires a paid plan.
  1343→+  </div>
  1344→+
  1345→+  <h3>Piper TTS (Offline Fallback)</h3>
  1346→+
  1347→+  <p>Fast local neural TTS system. C++ core with Python bindings. Runs entirely offline. MIT-licensed. Repository has been archived; development moved to <a href="https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl">piper1-gpl</a>.</p>
  1348→+
  1349→+  <ul>
  1350→+    <li>10.7k GitHub stars, well-established</li>
  1351→+    <li>Multiple voice models per language at different quality levels</li>
  1352→+    <li>Outputs raw PCM or WAV</li>
  1353→+    <li>Very fast -- suitable for real-time generation</li>
  1354→+    <li>Use from Node.js: shell out to the <code>piper</code> binary, pipe text in, get WAV out</li>
  1355→+  </ul>
  1356→+
  1357→+  <pre><code><span class="cm">// Shell out to piper from Node.js</span>
  1358→+<span class="kw">import</span> { execFile } <span class="kw">from</span> <span class="str">'child_process'</span>;
  1359→+
  1360→+<span class="kw">const</span> piper = execFile(<span class="str">'piper'</span>, [
  1361→+  <span class="str">'--model'</span>, <span class="str">'en_US-lessac-medium.onnx'</span>,
  1362→+  <span class="str">'--output_file'</span>, <span class="str">'/tmp/mic-break.wav'</span>
  1363→+]);
  1364→+piper.stdin.write(<span class="str">"Coming up next on the underground frequency..."</span>);
  1365→+piper.stdin.end();</code></pre>
  1366→+
  1367→+  <h3>say.js (System TTS Fallback)</h3>
  1368→+
  1369→+  <p>Uses platform-native TTS: macOS <code>say</code>, Windows SAPI, Linux Festival. Quality varies by platform -- macOS has decent neural voices, Linux Festival sounds robotic. Good as a zero-dependency fallback.</p>
  1370→+
  1371→+  <pre><code><span class="kw">import</span> say <span class="kw">from</span> <span class="str">'say'</span>;
  1372→+
  1373→+<span class="cm">// Speak aloud</span>
  1374→+say.speak(<span class="str">"You're listening to pirate radio."</span>, <span class="str">'Samantha'</span>, <span class="num">0.9</span>);
  1375→+
  1376→+<span class="cm">// Export to WAV (macOS/Windows only)</span>
  1377→+say.export(<span class="str">"Station identification."</span>, <span class="str">'Alex'</span>, <span class="num">0.85</span>, <span class="str">'/tmp/id.wav'</span>, (err) => {
  1378→+  <span class="cm">// file ready</span>
  1379→+});</code></pre>
  1380→+
  1381→+  <div class="callout warn">
  1382→+    <strong>Limitation:</strong> No export support on Linux. No streaming API. Limited voice quality on non-macOS platforms.
  1383→+  </div>
  1384→+
  1385→+  <h3>Mic Break Audio Pipeline</h3>
  1386→+
  1387→+  <p>The TTS output needs to be mixed into the radio stream. The cleanest approach is to generate TTS to a temp file, then have the playback engine duck the radio volume and play the mic break as an overlay or interstitial.</p>
  1388→+
  1389→+  <div class="mermaid">
  1390→+%%{init: {'theme': 'dark', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#1f3150', 'primaryTextColor': '#c9d1d9', 'primaryBorderColor': '#3d6ea5', 'lineColor': '#3d6ea5', 'secondaryColor': '#162030', 'tertiaryColor': '#11151c', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#0b0e14' }}}%%
  1391→+flowchart TD
  1392→+    A["Mic break trigger<br/>(timer / track change / manual)"] --> B["Generate TTS<br/>(Edge TTS / Piper)"]
  1393→+    B --> C["Save to temp .mp3"]
  1394→+    C --> D{"Playback strategy"}
  1395→+    D --> E["Duck radio volume<br/>(mpv volume command)"]
  1396→+    D --> F["Pause radio stream"]
  1397→+    E --> G["Play mic break<br/>(secondary mpv instance)"]
  1398→+    F --> G
  1399→+    G --> H["Restore radio<br/>(volume / resume)"]
  1400→+
  1401→+    style A fill:#162030,stroke:#3d6ea5,color:#c9d1d9
  1402→+    style B fill:#1f3150,stroke:#3d6ea5,color:#c9d1d9
  1403→+    style C fill:#162030,stroke:#3d6ea5,color:#c9d1d9
  1404→+    style D fill:#11151c,stroke:#e6a855,color:#c9d1d9
  1405→+    style E fill:#1f3150,stroke:#3d6ea5,color:#c9d1d9
  1406→+    style F fill:#1f3150,stroke:#3d6ea5,color:#c9d1d9
  1407→+    style G fill:#162030,stroke:#7ee6a8,color:#c9d1d9
  1408→+    style H fill:#11151c,stroke:#3d6ea5,color:#c9d1d9
  1409→+  </div>
  1410→+</section>
  1411→+
  1412→+<hr>
  1413→+
  1414→+<!-- =============== AUDIO PLAYBACK =============== -->
  1415→+<section id="audio-playback">
  1416→+  <h2>6. CLI Audio Playback</h2>
  1417→+
  1418→+  <h3>Option Comparison</h3>
  1419→+
  1420→+  <div class="table-wrap">
  1421→+    <table>
  1422→+      <thead><tr><th>Backend</th><th>Stream Support</th><th>IPC Control</th><th>Codec Support</th><th>Install</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
  1423→+      <tbody>
  1424→+        <tr>
  1425→+          <td><strong>mpv</strong></td>
  1426→+          <td>Excellent</td>
  1427→+          <td>JSON IPC socket</td>
  1428→+          <td>Everything</td>
  1429→+          <td><code>brew install mpv</code></td>
  1430→+          <td><span class="badge badge-rec">RECOMMENDED</span></td>
  1431→+        </tr>
  1432→+        <tr>
  1433→+          <td><strong>ffplay</strong></td>
  1434→+          <td>Good</td>
  1435→+          <td>None (stdin only)</td>
  1436→+          <td>Everything</td>
  1437→+          <td><code>brew install ffmpeg</code></td>
  1438→+          <td><span class="badge badge-todo">VIABLE</span></td>
  1439→+        </tr>
  1440→+        <tr>
  1441→+          <td><strong>sox/play</strong></td>
  1442→+          <td>Limited</td>
  1443→+          <td>None</td>

title:	fix: make /update work reliably in project venvs
state:	OPEN
author:	davetist
labels:	
assignees:	
reviewers:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	1435
url:	https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/1435
additions:	226
deletions:	32
auto-merge:	disabled
--
## Summary
- improve /update so the gateway can find and launch Hermes from the active venv
- pass the venv bin directory through PATH when spawning the detached update process
- make the updater detect both .venv and venv
- when uv is available, target the project venv explicitly with uv pip install --python
- if a project venv exists but pip is missing, bootstrap it with ensurepip before installing
- fall back to uv sync when no project venv is present
- add regression tests for both gateway launch behavior and updater dependency installation

## Why
/update could fail in venv and uv-managed setups for two related reasons:
- the gateway could launch the updater without the right executable/path context
- the updater could install into the wrong Python environment or fail if the local venv existed without pip

This makes the full /update flow more reliable for project-local virtualenv installs.

## Test plan
- python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_update_command.py -q
- python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_dependencies.py -q
- python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_delete.py -q
- manual verification with python -m hermes_cli.main update
```

This PR adds Cheri as an integration module inside Hermes Agent.

Cheri is a CLI-first collaborative workspace sync tool focused on:
- workspace-based collaboration
- file upload/download/list flows
- invite-based team access
- activity visibility
- task-based file and folder sync workflows

This PR introduces the initial Cheri integration structure inside the Hermes repository so it can be developed and tested as a modular component without mixing its code directly into unrelated Hermes subsystems.

   264→+def resolve_target_alias(config: GatewayConfig, target_agent: str, requester_session_key: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   265→+    collaboration_cfg = config.collaboration or {}
   266→+    targets = collaboration_cfg.get("targets", {}) if isinstance(collaboration_cfg, dict) else {}
   267→+    target = targets.get(target_agent)
   268→+    if not isinstance(target, dict):
   269→+        raise KeyError(f"Unknown collaboration target: {target_agent}")
   270→+    chat_id = str(target.get("chat_id", "")).strip()
   271→+    if not chat_id:
   272→+        raise ValueError(f"Target {target_agent} is missing chat_id")
   273→+    if requester_session_key.endswith(f"webhook:dm:{chat_id}"):
   274→+        raise ValueError("Cannot collaborate with the current session")
   275→+    return target

tool_result Bash

title:	feat(hooks): emit session:start and session:end lifecycle events
state:	OPEN
author:	bayrakdarerdem
labels:	
assignees:	
reviewers:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	1432
url:	https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/1432
additions:	12
deletions:	4
auto-merge:	disabled
--
**Summary**

The gateway hook system has had session:start listed in its documentation since day one — but it was never actually emitted. Any plugin author who wrote a hook listening for session:start would get silence. This PR fixes that disconnect and adds a companion session:end event that was also missing.


**Changes**
gateway/run.py

Emits session:start on the first message of a new session (detected by checking if transcript history is empty)
Emits session:end just before session:reset so hooks can clean up or persist data before the session is destroyed

gateway/hooks.py

Updated docstring to accurately list both new events
Clarified the distinction between session:end (session is closing) and session:reset (new session entry has been created)

**Why This Matters**
The hook system is designed for extensibility — plugins subscribe to lifecycle events and react accordingly. A session boundary is one of the most fundamental events in any agent system. Without session:start and session:end, plugins have no way to:

Initialize per-session state
Persist session analytics
Send welcome or goodbye messages
Clean up resources when a conversation ends

This is a small but foundational fix for the plugin ecosystem.
```

    63→+---
    64→+
    65→+## Technical design
    66→+
    67→+### Library: mautrix-python (not matrix-nio)
    68→+
    69→+matrix-nio was evaluated and found unsuitable for production E2EE bots:
    70→+- Cross-signing unimplemented since 2020 (issue #229, open, no activity)
    71→+- No reliable session persistence — every restart loses all Olm/Megolm sessions, causing "no session found" decrypt errors on every message after a restart
    72→+- Last maintained 2023
    73→+
    74→+mautrix-python is the library used by maubot and all production mautrix bridges. It has `PgCryptoStore` for proper persistence and active maintenance.
    75→+
    76→+### E2EE design (mirrors maubot)
    77→+
    78→+- **`PgCryptoStore` on SQLite** (`~/.hermes/matrix/crypto.db`) — all Olm/Megolm sessions, device keys, and cross-signing keys survive gateway restarts. This is the fundamental fix vs matrix-nio.
    79→+- **`resolve_trust()` guard** — cross-signing bootstrap runs once on first start only. All subsequent restarts skip it instantly via the local DB.
    80→+- **Recovery key auto-saved** to `~/.hermes/.env` on first bootstrap so device self-signing works on every restart.
    81→+- **Ghost device purge** — Synapse stores cross-signing public keys as device table rows. Without removal, Element tries to encrypt Olm messages to these phantom accounts and decryption fails. The adapter removes them on startup with UIA [REDACTED].
    82→+- **Encrypted media** — inbound files in E2EE rooms use `content.file.url` (not `content.url`) and require `decrypt_attachment` before caching. Both handled.
    83→+
    84→+### Python 3.14 compatibility
    85→+
    86→+mautrix 0.21.0 has five incompatibilities with Python 3.14. `_patch_mautrix_py314()` applies targeted monkey-patches at import time, no-op on Python < 3.14. Two patches fix real mautrix bugs on all Python versions and run unconditionally.
    87→+
    88→+### Media support
    89→+
    90→+**Outbound** — all methods use correct base-class parameter names and upload via `/_matrix/media/v3/upload`. Supports `send_image`, `send_image_file`, `send_animation`, `send_voice`, `send_video`, `send_document`. Accepts local paths or existing `mxc://` URIs.
    91→+
    92→+**Inbound** — mautrix msgtype strings (`"m.image"`, `"m.audio"`, `"m.video"`, `"m.file"`) compared as strings. Downloads, decrypts if E2EE, caches, and populates `event.media_urls`/`event.media_types` following the Telegram adapter pattern exactly. Agent sees files via the standard document context note.
    93→+
    94→+### Typing indicators
    95→+
    96→+`send_typing()` → `PUT /rooms/{id}/typing` with 20s keepalive (Matrix typing expires at 30s). Clears in `send_message()`. Same pattern as nanobot's Matrix implementation.
    97→+
    98→+### Setup wizard (zero manual steps)
    99→+
   100→+`hermes gateway setup matrix`:
   101→+1. Homeserver URL + SSL + live connectivity test
   102→+2. Bot user ID
   103→+3. Bot password → logs in automatically, gets token + device ID (no curl commands)
   104→+4. E2EE deps checked/installed
   105→+5. Cross-signing bootstrap inline, recovery key auto-saved
   106→+6. Allowed users
   107→+7. Trust verification inline — signs bot's master key from each allowed user's account
   108→+
   109→+Re-configuration: wizard offers to wipe all E2EE state for a clean start.
   110→+
   111→+---
   112→+
   113→+## Known limitations
   114→+
   115→+1. **`_send_matrix()` tool does not support E2EE** — one-shot HTTP client, no sync loop. Messages to encrypted rooms will fail. Documented with warning log. The running gateway handles E2EE correctly; this only affects the standalone tool.
   116→+
   117→+2. **SAS verification** — implemented via `olm.Sas` directly (mautrix 0.21.0 lacks built-in SAS). Tested with Element Desktop only.
   118→+
   119→+3. **No explicit sync reconnection backoff** — mautrix's `client.start()` has internal retry but no configurable backoff wrapper.
   120→+
   121→+---
   122→+
   123→+## Testing
   124→+
   125→+### Tested against
   126→+- **Synapse** self-hosted on k3s (v1.99+), self-signed TLS via Tailscale
   127→+- **Element Desktop** on Arch Linux
   128→+- **Python 3.14**
   129→+- **Media** — image, audio, document upload/download verified live against Synapse
   130→+
   131→+### k8s / self-hosted note
   132→+If media upload returns `500 Internal server error`, the `media_store` volume may be owned by root. Fix:
   133→+```bash
   134→+kubectl exec -n matrix <pod> -- chown -R 991:991 /data/media_store
   135→+```
   136→+The standard Synapse k8s init container handles this on every pod start, but pre-existing volumes may need a one-time manual fix.
   137→+
   138→+### Needs community validation
   139→+- **matrix.org** (public homeserver) — rate limits and UIA behavior may differ
   140→+- **Dendrite** — different cross-signing implementation
   141→+- **Element X** (Rust SDK) — different verification flow
   142→+- **Python 3.11 / 3.12** — patches are no-ops; should work but unconfirmed
   143→+- **Other clients** (FluffyChat, Nheko, Cinny) — untested
   144→+
   145→+### How to test
   146→+
   147→+```bash
   148→+# Install E2EE dependencies
   149→+# Setup wizard does handle this and install if not available
   150→+pip install "mautrix[e2be]" asyncpg aiosqlite base58
   151→+sudo pacman -S libolm   # Arch; or: apt install libolm-dev
   152→+
   153→+# Full guided setup (wizard handles everything)
   154→+hermes gateway setup
   155→+# select matrix (6)
   156→+
   157→+# Start
   158→+hermes gateway restart
   159→+
   160→+# Send a text message, image, PDF in Element — bot should respond
   161→+# If trust verification incomplete:
   162→+hermes gateway verify-matrix
   163→+```
   164→+
   165→+### Test results
   166→+```
   167→+93 passed  (tests/gateway/test_matrix.py)
   168→+3550 passed total — same 35 pre-existing failures as main, zero regressions
   169→+```
   170→+
   171→+---
   172→+
   173→+## Environment variables
   174→+
   175→+| Variable | Required | Description |
   176→+|----------|----------|-------------|
   177→+| `MATRIX_HOMESERVER_URL` | Yes | e.g. `https://matrix.example.org` |
   178→+| `MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | Bot account access token (`syt_...`) |
   179→+| `MATRIX_USER_ID` | Yes | Bot Matrix ID (`@bot:example.org`) |
   180→+| `MATRIX_DEVICE_ID` | Recommended | Pins to one device; prevents session replay on restart |
   181→+| `MATRIX_ALLOWED_USERS` | Recommended | Comma-separated IDs allowed to message the bot |
   182→+| `MATRIX_HOME_CHANNEL` | Optional | Room ID for cron job delivery |
   183→+| `MATRIX_HOME_CHANNEL_NAME` | Optional | Display name for home channel (default: "Home") |
   184→+| `MATRIX_VERIFY_SSL` | Optional | `false` for self-signed TLS (default `true`) |
   185→+| `MATRIX_E2EE` | Optional | `true` for E2EE (requires deps above) |
   186→+| `MATRIX_PASSWORD` | Optional | Bot password for cross-signing UIA fallback |
   187→+| `MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY` | Optional | Auto-saved by gateway; enables device self-signing on restart |
   188→+
   189→+## Dependencies
   190→+
   191→+All optional — only needed when `MATRIX_E2EE=true`. Installed automatically by the setup wizard.
   192→+
   193→+| Package | Purpose |
   194→+|---------|---------|
   195→+| `mautrix[e2be]` | Matrix client + E2EE crypto |
   196→+| `asyncpg` | SQL dialect for `PgCryptoStore` |
   197→+| `aiosqlite` | SQLite backend (no PostgreSQL needed) |
   198→+| `base58` | Recovery key encoding |
   199→+| `libolm` | Olm/Megolm C library (system package) |
   200→+

  1578→+<span class="kw">const</span> speaker = <span class="kw">new</span> Speaker({
  1579→+  channels: <span class="num">2</span>,
  1580→+  bitDepth: <span class="num">16</span>,
  1581→+  sampleRate: <span class="num">44100</span>,
  1582→+  signed: <span class="kw">true</span>,
  1583→+});
  1584→+
  1585→+<span class="cm">// Pipe decoded PCM audio to speakers</span>
  1586→+decodedStream.pipe(speaker);
  1587→+
  1588→+<span class="cm">// Events: "open", "flush", "close"</span>
  1589→+
  1590→+<span class="cm">// Supported backends: ALSA (Linux), CoreAudio (macOS), winmm (Windows)</span></code></pre>
  1591→+
  1592→+  <div class="callout warn">
  1593→+    <strong>Why not node-speaker for radio:</strong> It only accepts raw PCM, meaning you'd need to separately decode MP3/AAC/Ogg streams. It also requires native compilation (node-gyp), and mixing multiple audio sources (radio + TTS) would require manual PCM buffer interleaving. mpv handles all of this transparently.
  1594→+  </div>
  1595→+
  1596→+  <h3>play-sound (Simple File Playback)</h3>
  1597→+
  1598→+  <p>Thin wrapper that spawns a system audio player to play a file. Auto-detects available players: <code>mplayer</code>, <code>afplay</code> (macOS), <code>mpg123</code>, <code>play</code> (sox), <code>cvlc</code>, etc. Useful for one-shot sound effects but not for streaming radio.</p>
  1599→+</section>
  1600→+
  1601→+<hr>
  1602→+
  1603→+<!-- =============== ARCHITECTURE =============== -->
  1604→+<section id="architecture">
  1605→+  <h2>7. Recommended Architecture</h2>
  1606→+
  1607→+  <div class="mermaid">
  1608→+%%{init: {'theme': 'dark', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#1f3150', 'primaryTextColor': '#c9d1d9', 'primaryBorderColor': '#3d6ea5', 'lineColor': '#3d6ea5', 'secondaryColor': '#162030', 'tertiaryColor': '#11151c', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#0b0e14' }}}%%
  1609→+flowchart TD

  1611→+

  1645→+
  1646→+  <h3>Key Architectural Decisions</h3>
  1647→+
  1648→+  <ul>
  1649→+    <li><strong>mpv as playback backend:</strong> External process controlled via JSON IPC. Handles all codec/protocol complexity. Two instances enable radio + voice overlay without interruption</li>
  1650→+    <li><strong>Station aggregation at startup:</strong> Fetch SomaFM channels.json and cache. Lazy-load Radio Browser searches. Parse Icecast yp.xml once and cache. Merge into unified station model</li>
  1651→+    <li><strong>TTS with graceful degradation:</strong> Try Edge TTS first (best quality, free). Fall back to Piper if offline. Last resort: system TTS via say.js</li>
  1652→+    <li><strong>Mic break scheduling:</strong> Timer-based (every N minutes), event-driven (on track change detected via mpv metadata events), or manual trigger. Pre-generate next announcement during playback for zero-latency transitions</li>
  1653→+    <li><strong>Announcement templates:</strong> Parameterized strings with station name, current track, time, listener count. Vary phrases to avoid repetition. Possible LLM integration for dynamic DJ patter</li>
  1654→+  </ul>
  1655→+
  1656→+  <h3>Dependency Stack</h3>
  1657→+  <pre><code><span class="cm">// Core</span>
  1658→+<span class="str">"node-mpv"</span>: <span class="str">"^1.5.0"</span>          <span class="cm">// mpv IPC wrapper (zero deps)</span>
  1659→+
  1660→+<span class="cm">// TTS (pick one or layer them)</span>
  1661→+<span class="str">"@bestcodes/edge-tts"</span>: <span class="str">"^3.0"</span>  <span class="cm">// MIT, clean API, &lt;50kb</span>
  1662→+<span class="cm">// OR</span>
  1663→+<span class="str">"@andresaya/edge-tts"</span>: <span class="str">"^1.8"</span>  <span class="cm">// GPL-3, more features/formats</span>
  1664→+
  1665→+<span class="cm">// System requirement</span>
  1666→+<span class="cm">// mpv must be installed: brew install mpv</span></code></pre>
  1667→+</section>
  1668→+
  1669→+<hr>
  1670→+
  1671→+<!-- =============== RECOMMENDATIONS =============== -->
  1672→+<section id="recommendations">
  1673→+  <h2>8. Final Recommendations</h2>
  1674→+
  1675→+  <ul class="checklist">
  1676→+    <li class="done"><strong>Radio streams:</strong> Radio Browser API as primary discovery engine (45k+ stations, excellent search). SomaFM as curated preset collection. Icecast directory as supplementary source</li>
  1677→+    <li class="done"><strong>Audio playback:</strong> mpv via node-mpv wrapper. Two instances (radio + voice). JSON IPC gives full programmatic control including volume, metadata, pause, stream switching</li>
  1678→+    <li class="done"><strong>TTS engine:</strong> Edge TTS as default (free, neural quality, 400+ voices, no API key). Support ElevenLabs as premium upgrade path. Piper as offline fallback</li>
  1679→+    <li class="done"><strong>Mic break flow:</strong> Generate TTS to temp file, duck radio volume via mpv IPC, play announcement on secondary mpv instance, restore volume on completion</li>
  1680→+    <li class="done"><strong>Pre-generation:</strong> Generate next mic break during playback to eliminate latency. Cache generated audio for repeated announcements (station IDs, time checks)</li>
  1681→+  </ul>
  1682→+
  1683→+  <h3>Key Trade-offs</h3>
  1684→+
  1685→+  <div class="compare">
  1686→+    <div class="compare-card">
  1687→+      <h4>mpv (external process)</h4>
  1688→+      <ul>
  1689→+        <li>Pro: handles all codecs/protocols</li>
  1690→+        <li>Pro: rich IPC for full control</li>
  1691→+        <li>Pro: battle-tested reliability</li>
  1692→+        <li>Con: requires system install</li>
  1693→+        <li>Con: two processes for overlay</li>
  1694→+      </ul>
  1695→+    </div>
  1696→+    <div class="compare-card after">
  1697→+      <h4>node-speaker (in-process)</h4>
  1698→+      <ul>
  1699→+        <li>Pro: no external dependency</li>
  1700→+        <li>Pro: fine-grained PCM mixing</li>
  1701→+        <li>Con: must decode all formats</li>
  1702→+        <li>Con: native compilation</li>
  1703→+        <li>Con: manual buffer management</li>
  1704→+      </ul>
  1705→+    </div>
  1706→+  </div>
  1707→+
  1708→+  <div class="compare">
  1709→+    <div class="compare-card">
  1710→+      <h4>Edge TTS (online)</h4>
  1711→+      <ul>
  1712→+        <li>Pro: free, no API key</li>
  1713→+        <li>Pro: neural quality voices</li>
  1714→+        <li>Pro: 400+ voices, 100+ languages</li>
  1715→+        <li>Con: requires internet</li>
  1716→+        <li>Con: unofficial API, could break</li>
  1717→+      </ul>
  1718→+    </div>
  1719→+    <div class="compare-card after">
  1720→+      <h4>ElevenLabs (premium)</h4>
  1721→+      <ul>
  1722→+        <li>Pro: best voice quality</li>
  1723→+        <li>Pro: voice cloning</li>
  1724→+        <li>Pro: official stable API</li>
  1725→+        <li>Con: costs money</li>
  1726→+        <li>Con: rate limits</li>
  1727→+      </ul>
  1728→+    </div>
  1729→+  </div>
  1730→+
  1731→+  <div class="callout success">
  1732→+    <strong>Minimum viable stack:</strong> <code>node-mpv</code> + <code>@bestcodes/edge-tts</code> + Radio Browser API. Two npm packages, one system dependency (mpv), zero API keys. This gets you streaming radio with DJ mic breaks in a minimal, maintainable setup.
  1733→+  </div>

  1766→+# CLI Radio Player: Technical Research
  1767→+
  1768→+> Technical research for a CLI pirate radio player with TTS mic breaks and internet radio station aggregation.
  1769→+
  1770→+**Stack:** TypeScript / Node.js
  1771→+**Date:** 2026-03-14
  1772→+
  1773→+---
  1774→+
  1775→+## Contents
  1776→+
  1777→+1. [Radio Station Directories](#1-radio-station-directories)
  1778→+2. [SomaFM API](#2-somafm-api)
  1779→+3. [Radio Browser API](#3-radio-browser-api)
  1780→+4. [Icecast Directory](#4-icecast-directory-dirxiphorg)
  1781→+5. [TTS for Mic Breaks](#5-tts-for-mic-breaks)
  1782→+6. [CLI Audio Playback](#6-cli-audio-playback)
  1783→+7. [Recommended Architecture](#7-recommended-architecture)
  1784→+8. [Final Recommendations](#8-final-recommendations)
  1785→+
  1786→+---
  1787→+
  1788→+## 1. Radio Station Directories
  1789→+
  1790→+Three primary open directories provide API access to internet radio streams. Between them you get coverage of curated indie stations, the entire long tail of community radio, and the Icecast/Shoutcast ecosystem.
  1791→+
  1792→+| Directory     | Stations    | Auth | Format                | Character                              |
  1793→+|---------------|-------------|------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------|
  1794→+| SomaFM        | ~40 curated | None | JSON                  | High-quality curated indie/underground |
  1795→+| Radio Browser | 45,000+     | None | JSON/XML/CSV/M3U/PLS  | Community-maintained global directory  |
  1796→+| Icecast       | ~350+       | None | XML (yp.xml)          | Icecast-native stations, many underground |
  1797→+
  1798→+---
  1799→+
  1800→+## 2. SomaFM API
  1801→+
  1802→+SomaFM is a listener-supported, commercial-free internet radio service based in San Francisco. It runs ~40 curated channels spanning ambient, electronic, indie, lounge, metal, and experimental genres. The aesthetic is perfect for a pirate radio vibe.
  1803→+
  1804→+### Channels Endpoint
  1805→+
  1806→+```
  1807→+GET https://api.somafm.com/channels.json
  1808→+```
  1809→+
  1810→+No authentication, no rate limiting documented.
  1811→+
  1812→+### Channel Object Structure
  1813→+
  1814→+```json
  1815→+{
  1816→+  "id": "groovesalad",
  1817→+  "title": "Groove Salad",
  1818→+  "description": "A nicely chilled plate of ambient/downtempo...",
  1819→+  "genre": "ambient|electronic",         // pipe-separated
  1820→+  "dj": "Rusty",
  1821→+  "djmail": "[REDACTED]",
  1822→+  "lastPlaying": "Artist - Track",       // current/recent track
  1823→+  "listeners": "1234",                   // string, not number
  1824→+  "image": "https://...",                // 120px thumbnail
  1825→+  "largeimage": "https://...",           // 256px
  1826→+  "xlimage": "https://...",              // 512px
  1827→+  "playlists": [
  1828→+    { "url": "https://somafm.com/groovesalad130.pls", "format": "aac", "quality": "highest" },
  1829→+    { "url": "https://somafm.com/groovesalad.pls",    "format": "mp3", "quality": "high" },
  1830→+    { "url": "https://somafm.com/groovesalad32.pls",  "format": "aacp", "quality": "low" }
  1831→+  ]
  1832→+}
  1833→+```
  1834→+
  1835→+### Stream URL Patterns
  1836→+
  1837→+| Pattern                           | Format       | Example                    |
  1838→+|-----------------------------------|--------------|----------------------------|
  1839→+| `/{channel}{bitrate}.pls`         | PLS playlist | `/groovesalad130.pls`      |
  1840→+| `/m3u/{channel}{bitrate}.m3u`     | M3U playlist | `/m3u/groovesalad130.m3u`  |
  1841→+| `/nossl/{channel}{bitrate}.pls`   | PLS (HTTP)   | `/nossl/groovesalad130.pls`|
  1842→+
  1843→+### Notable Channels for Pirate Radio Vibe
  1844→+
  1845→+- `defcon` -- Music for hacking. Dark, edgy electronic
  1846→+- `darkzone` -- Dark ambient, industrial
  1847→+- `doomed` -- Dark industrial/ambient
  1848→+- `sf1033` -- Ambient with SF police scanner overlay
  1849→+- `vaporwaves` -- Vaporwave aesthetics
  1850→+- `cliqhop` -- Intelligent dance music
  1851→+- `fluid` -- Instrumental hip-hop
  1852→+- `dubstep` -- Dubstep/deep bass
  1853→+- `thetrip` -- Progressive house/trance
  1854→+- `digitalis` -- Experimental electronic rock
  1855→+
  1856→+> **Advantage:** SomaFM streams are high quality, reliable, and legal. The PLS files resolve to direct Icecast stream URLs that mpv can play natively. Song history available at `/{channel}/songhistory.html`.
  1857→+
  1858→+---
  1859→+
  1860→+## 3. Radio Browser API
  1861→+
  1862→+The largest open directory of internet radio stations. Community-maintained, free, no auth required. Over 45,000 stations indexed with full metadata. This is the backbone for station discovery.
  1863→+
  1864→+### Server Discovery
  1865→+
  1866→+The API runs on multiple mirrors. Resolve `all.api.radio-browser.info` via DNS to get a list of available servers, then pick one at random for load balancing.
  1867→+
  1868→+```ts
  1869→+// Discover servers via DNS
  1870→+const { resolve } = require('dns/promises');
  1871→+const servers = await resolve('all.api.radio-browser.info');
  1872→+// Use: https://{server}/json/stations/search
  1873→+```
  1874→+
  1875→+### Key Endpoints
  1876→+
  1877→+#### Search Stations
  1878→+
  1879→+```
  1880→+GET/POST /{format}/stations/search
  1881→+
  1882→+Parameters (all optional):
  1883→+  name          -- station name (fuzzy)
  1884→+  nameExact     -- exact match
  1885→+  tag           -- single genre tag
  1886→+  tagList       -- comma-separated tags (AND)
  1887→+  country       -- full country name
  1888→+  countrycode   -- ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
  1889→+  language      -- language name
  1890→+  codec         -- audio codec (mp3, aac, ogg...)
  1891→+  bitrateMin    -- minimum kbps
  1892→+  bitrateMax    -- maximum kbps
  1893→+  is_https      -- HTTPS-only streams
  1894→+  order         -- name|votes|clickcount|bitrate|random
  1895→+  limit         -- results per page
  1896→+  offset        -- pagination
  1897→+  hidebroken    -- exclude offline stations
  1898→+```
  1899→+
  1900→+#### Curated Lists
  1901→+
  1902→+```
  1903→+GET /json/stations/topclick/{limit}      -- most popular
  1904→+GET /json/stations/topvote/{limit}       -- highest rated
  1905→+GET /json/stations/lastclick/{limit}     -- recently played
  1906→+GET /json/stations/lastchange/{limit}    -- recently added
  1907→+GET /json/stations/search?order=random   -- random discovery
  1908→+```
  1909→+
  1910→+#### Browse Metadata
  1911→+
  1912→+```
  1913→+GET /json/tags          -- all genre tags with counts
  1914→+GET /json/countries     -- all countries with counts
  1915→+GET /json/languages     -- all languages with counts
  1916→+GET /json/codecs        -- all codecs with counts
  1917→+```
  1918→+
  1919→+#### Get Resolved Stream URL
  1920→+
  1921→+```
  1922→+GET /json/url/{stationuuid}
  1923→+
  1924→+Returns:
  1925→+{
  1926→+  "url": "https://original.url/stream",
  1927→+  "url_resolved": "https://actual.server/stream.mp3",  // direct stream
  1928→+  "stationuuid": "abc-123-def"
  1929→+}
  1930→+// Also increments the station's click counter
  1931→+```
  1932→+
  1933→+### Station Object
  1934→+
  1935→+```json
  1936→+{
  1937→+  "stationuuid": "abc-123",
  1938→+  "name": "Underground FM",
  1939→+  "url": "https://stream.example.com/radio",
  1940→+  "url_resolved": "https://...",
  1941→+  "homepage": "https://...",
  1942→+  "favicon": "https://...",
  1943→+  "tags": "electronic,underground,pirate",
  1944→+  "country": "United States",
  1945→+  "countrycode": "US",
  1946→+  "language": "english",
  1947→+  "codec": "MP3",
  1948→+  "bitrate": 128,
  1949→+  "votes": 42,
  1950→+  "clickcount": 1337,
  1951→+  "lastcheckok": 1,
  1952→+  "hls": 0,
  1953→+  "geo_lat": 37.7749,
  1954→+  "geo_long": -122.4194
  1955→+}
  1956→+```
  1957→+
  1958→+> **Usage Notes:** Set a descriptive `User-Agent` header. Use `url_resolved` for direct playback (bypasses playlist file parsing). Click counting is limited to once per IP per station per day. All GET params can be sent as POST with JSON body.
  1959→+
  1960→+### Useful Tag Searches for Pirate Radio
  1961→+
  1962→+```
  1963→+"pirate", "underground", "independent", "college", "community",
  1964→+"freeform", "experimental", "lo-fi", "punk", "diy",
  1965→+"noise", "avant-garde", "alternative", "anarchist"
  1966→+```
  1967→+
  1968→+---
  1969→+
  1970→+## 4. Icecast Directory (dir.xiph.org)
  1971→+
  1972→+The Xiph.org Icecast directory provides a machine-readable XML feed of Icecast-registered stations. Smaller than Radio Browser but contains stations that may not appear elsewhere, particularly hobbyist and underground broadcasters.
  1973→+
  1974→+### Endpoint
  1975→+
  1976→+```
  1977→+GET https://dir.xiph.org/yp.xml
  1978→+```
  1979→+
  1980→+### Entry Structure
  1981→+
  1982→+```xml
  1983→+<entry>
  1984→+  <server_name>Underground Radio</server_name>
  1985→+  <server_type>audio/mpeg</server_type>
  1986→+  <bitrate>128</bitrate>
  1987→+  <samplerate>44100</samplerate>
  1988→+  <channels>2</channels>
  1989→+  <listen_url>https://stream.example.com/radio</listen_url>
  1990→+  <current_song>Artist - Track</current_song>
  1991→+  <genre>electronic experimental</genre>
  1992→+</entry>
  1993→+```
  1994→+
  1995→+Audio formats include `audio/mpeg` (MP3), `audio/aac`, `audio/aacp`, `application/ogg`, and `audio/mp4`. Bitrates range from 16 kbps (talk/scanner) to 1024 kbps (high-fidelity music). The `listen_url` values are direct stream URLs -- no playlist resolution needed.
  1996→+
  1997→+> **Limitation:** The Icecast directory is a flat XML file with no search/filter API. You must fetch the entire file and filter client-side. Best treated as a supplementary source parsed on startup and cached.
  1998→+
  1999→+---
```

   214→+#!/usr/bin/env python3
   215→+"""
   216→+Demo: Raw tool output WITHOUT Execution Integrity Layer.
   217→+
   218→+Shows the same 17 scenarios as demo_execution_verifier.py but returns
   219→+raw tool output with NO _verification or _warning fields — this is
   220→+what the model sees when the verifier is disabled.
   221→+
   222→+Compare side-by-side:
   223→+    python3 demo_without_verifier.py   # raw output (before)
   224→+    python3 demo_execution_verifier.py # augmented output (after)
   225→+"""
   226→+
   227→+import json
   228→+import os
   229→+import tempfile
   230→+from pathlib import Path
   231→+
   232→+
   233→+def _pp(label: str, result_json: str):
   234→+    """Pretty-print a raw tool result."""
   235→+    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
   236→+    print(f"  {label}")
   237→+    print(f"{'='*60}")
   238→+    try:
   239→+        data = json.loads(result_json)
   240→+        print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
   241→+    except json.JSONDecodeError:
   242→+        print(result_json)
   243→+
   244→+
   245→+def main():
   246→+    print("Raw Tool Output — No Verification (Before)")
   247→+    print("Same 17 scenarios, but the model gets ONLY the tool's own JSON.\n")
   248→+
   249→+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hermes-demo-") as tmpdir:
   250→+
   251→+        # ── 1. git clone — SUCCESS ─────────────────────────────────────
   252→+        clone_dir = os.path.join(tmpdir, "my-project")
   253→+        os.makedirs(clone_dir)  # simulate successful clone
   254→+
   255→+        result = json.dumps({"output": "Cloning into 'my-project'...\ndone.", "exit_code": 0, "error": None})
   256→+        _pp("1. git clone — directory EXISTS (no verification)", result)
   257→+
   258→+        # ── 2. git clone — FAILURE ─────────────────────────────────────
   259→+        result = json.dumps({"output": "Cloning into 'ghost-repo'...\ndone.", "exit_code": 0, "error": None})
   260→+        _pp("2. git clone — directory MISSING (no verification)", result)
   261→+
   262→+        # ── 3. write_file — SUCCESS ────────────────────────────────────
   263→+        written_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, "hello.py")
   264→+        Path(written_file).write_text("print('hello world')\n")
   265→+
   266→+        result = json.dumps({"bytes_written": 21})
   267→+        _pp("3. write_file — file EXISTS and non-empty (no verification)", result)
   268→+
   269→+        # ── 4. write_file — EMPTY FILE (intentional) ──────────────────
   270→+        empty_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, "empty.txt")
   271→+        Path(empty_file).write_text("")
   272→+
   273→+        result = json.dumps({"bytes_written": 0})
   274→+        _pp("4. write_file — file EXISTS, intentionally empty (no verification)", result)
   275→+
   276→+        # ── 5. write_file — MISSING FILE ───────────────────────────────
   277→+        result = json.dumps({"bytes_written": 3})
   278→+        _pp("5. write_file — file MISSING after write (no verification)", result)
   279→+
   280→+        # ── 6. patch — SUCCESS ─────────────────────────────────────────
   281→+        patched_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, "app.py")
   282→+        Path(patched_file).write_text("x = 2\n")
   283→+
   284→+        result = json.dumps({"success": True, "diff": "- x = 1\n+ x = 2", "files_modified": [patched_file]})
   285→+        _pp("6. patch — modified file EXISTS (no verification)", result)
   286→+
   287→+        # ── 7. patch — MISSING AFTER PATCH ──────────────────────────────
   288→+        deleted_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "deleted.py")
   289→+        result = json.dumps({"success": True, "diff": "...", "files_modified": [deleted_path]})
   290→+        _pp("7. patch — modified file MISSING (no verification)", result)
   291→+
   292→+        # ── 8. Unrelated tool — passthrough ─────────────────────────────
   293→+        result = json.dumps({"results": [{"title": "asyncio docs", "url": "https://..."}]})
   294→+        _pp("8. web_search — passthrough (no verification)", result)
   295→+
   296→+        # ── 9. terminal cp — destination EXISTS ─────────────────────────
   297→+        result = json.dumps({"output": "", "exit_code": 0, "error": None})
   298→+        _pp("9. terminal cp — destination EXISTS (no verification)", result)
   299→+
   300→+        # ── 10. terminal rm — target REMOVED ────────────────────────────
   301→+        result = json.dumps({"output": "", "exit_code": 0, "error": None})
   302→+        _pp("10. terminal rm — target REMOVED (no verification)", result)
   303→+
   304→+        # ── 11. terminal touch — file EXISTS ────────────────────────────
   305→+        result = json.dumps({"output": "", "exit_code": 0, "error": None})
   306→+        _pp("11. terminal touch — file EXISTS (no verification)", result)
   307→+
   308→+        # ── 12. terminal git init — .git EXISTS ─────────────────────────
   309→+        result = json.dumps({"output": "Initialized empty Git repository", "exit_code": 0, "error": None})
   310→+        _pp("12. terminal git init — .git EXISTS (no verification)", result)
   311→+
   312→+        # ── 13. read_file — content returned ────────────────────────────
   313→+        result = json.dumps({"content": "1|print('hello')\n2|print('world')", "total_lines": 2, "file_size": 28, "error": None})
   314→+        _pp("13. read_file — content returned (no verification)", result)
   315→+
   316→+        # ── 14. read_file — error with similar_files ────────────────────
   317→+        result = json.dumps({"error": "File not found: /tmp/foo.py", "similar_files": ["/tmp/foo2.py", "/tmp/foobar.py"]})
   318→+        _pp("14. read_file — error with similar_files (no verification)", result)
   319→+
   320→+        # ── 15. browser_navigate — success ──────────────────────────────
   321→+        result = json.dumps({"success": True, "url": "https://example.com", "title": "Example Domain"})
   322→+        _pp("15. browser_navigate — success (no verification)", result)
   323→+
   324→+        # ── 16. browser_navigate — bot detection ────────────────────────
   325→+        result = json.dumps({
   326→+            "success": True,
   327→+            "url": "https://protected-site.com",
   328→+            "title": "Verify you are human",
   329→+            "bot_detection_warning": "Page title suggests bot detection",
   330→+        })
   331→+        _pp("16. browser_navigate — bot detection triggered (no verification)", result)
   332→+
   333→+        # ── 17. web_extract — partial failure ───────────────────────────
   334→+        result = json.dumps({"results": [
   335→+            {"url": "https://a.com", "title": "A", "content": "Page A content extracted successfully."},
   336→+            {"url": "https://b.com", "error": "Connection timeout", "content": ""},
   337→+        ]})
   338→+        _pp("17. web_extract — partial failure (no verification)", result)
   339→+
   340→+    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
   341→+    print("  Demo complete. Notice: NO _verification or _warning fields.")
   342→+    print("  The model has no signal that scenarios 2, 5, 7, 14, 16, 17")
   343→+    print("  had issues requiring attention.")
   344→+    print(f"{'='*60}\n")
   345→+
   346→+
   347→+if __name__ == "__main__":
   348→+    main()

   381→+"""Tests for agent.execution_verifier — post-tool-call verification."""
   382→+
   383→+import json
   384→+import os
   385→+import tempfile
   386→+
   387→+import pytest
   388→+
   389→+from agent.execution_verifier import (
   390→+    VerificationResult,
   391→+    verify_tool_result,
   392→+    _verify_terminal,
   393→+    _verify_write_file,
   394→+    _verify_patch,
   395→+    _verify_read_file,
   396→+    _verify_browser_navigate,
   397→+    _verify_web_extract,
   398→+    VERIFIED,
   399→+    WARNING,
   400→+    MISMATCH,
   401→+)
   402→+
   403→+
   404→+# ===================================================================
   405→+# VerificationResult
   406→+# ===================================================================
   407→+
   408→+class TestVerificationResult:
   409→+    def test_to_dict_verified(self):
   410→+        vr = VerificationResult(
   411→+            status=VERIFIED, tool_name="terminal", check="git_clone_dir_exists",
   412→+        )
   413→+        d = vr.to_dict()
   414→+        assert d["status"] == "verified"
   415→+        assert d["tool"] == "terminal"
   416→+        assert d["check"] == "git_clone_dir_exists"
   417→+        assert "message" not in d  # empty message excluded
   418→+
   419→+    def test_to_dict_mismatch_includes_message(self):
   420→+        vr = VerificationResult(
   421→+            status=MISMATCH, tool_name="write_file", check="file_written",
   422→+            message="written file does not exist: /tmp/foo.py",
   423→+            details={"expected_path": "/tmp/foo.py", "exists": False},
   424→+        )
   425→+        d = vr.to_dict()
   426→+        assert d["status"] == "mismatch"
   427→+        assert "does not exist" in d["message"]
   428→+        assert d["details"]["exists"] is False
   429→+
   430→+    def test_to_dict_warning(self):
   431→+        vr = VerificationResult(
   432→+            status=WARNING, tool_name="write_file", check="file_written",
   433→+            message="file exists but is empty despite non-empty content arg: /tmp/empty.txt",
   434→+        )
   435→+        d = vr.to_dict()
   436→+        assert d["status"] == "warning"
   437→+        assert "empty" in d["message"]
   438→+
   439→+
   440→+# ===================================================================
   441→+# Terminal verifier
   442→+# ===================================================================
   443→+
   444→+class TestTerminalVerifier:
   445→+    # --- git clone ---
   446→+
   447→+    def test_git_clone_with_explicit_dir_exists(self, tmp_path):
   448→+        target = tmp_path / "myrepo"
   449→+        target.mkdir()
   450→+        args = {"command": f"git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git {target}"}
   451→+        result_data = {"output": "Cloning...", "exit_code": 0, "error": None}
   452→+        vr = _verify_terminal(args, result_data)
   453→+        assert vr is not None
   454→+        assert vr.status == VERIFIED
   455→+        assert vr.check == "git_clone_dir_exists"
   456→+
   457→+    def test_git_clone_with_explicit_dir_missing(self, tmp_path):
   458→+        target = tmp_path / "nonexistent"
   459→+        args = {"command": f"git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git {target}"}
   460→+        result_data = {"output": "Cloning...", "exit_code": 0, "error": None}
   461→+        vr = _verify_terminal(args, result_data)
   462→+        assert vr is not None
   463→+        assert vr.status == MISMATCH
   464→+        assert "does not exist" in vr.message
   465→+
   466→+    def test_git_clone_inferred_dir_exists(self, tmp_path):
   467→+        target = tmp_path / "my-project"
   468→+        target.mkdir()
   469→+        args = {
   470→+            "command": "git clone https://github.com/user/my-project.git",
   471→+            "workdir": str(tmp_path),
   472→+        }
   473→+        result_data = {"output": "Cloning...", "exit_code": 0, "error": None}
   474→+        vr = _verify_terminal(args, result_data)
   475→+        assert vr is not None
   476→+        assert vr.status == VERIFIED
   477→+
   478→+    def test_git_clone_inferred_dir_missing(self, tmp_path):
   479→+        args = {
   480→+            "command": "git clone https://github.com/user/my-project.git",
   481→+            "workdir": str(tmp_path),
   482→+        }
   483→+        result_data = {"output": "Cloning...", "exit_code": 0, "error": None}
   484→+        vr = _verify_terminal(args, result_data)
   485→+        assert vr is not None
   486→+        assert vr.status == MISMATCH
   487→+

   946→+class TestVerifyToolResult:
   947→+    def test_augments_terminal_result(self, tmp_path):

   953→+        parsed = json.loads(result)

   958→+    def test_augments_write_file_result(self, tmp_path):

Here is my review of PR #1467.

---

## PR #1467: Improve error logging in terminal tool

**Author:** aydnOktay | **Branch:** `improve/terminal-error-logging` -> `main` | **Size:** +11 / -10 (small) | **CI:** All checks passing

### Summary

This PR adds `exc_info=True` to 11 logging calls in `tools/terminal_tool.py`. This causes Python's logging module to append the full stack trace to each log message, improving debuggability when errors occur. The locations touched are:

- File stat errors in disk usage check (`debug`)
- Terminal attribute restoration / tty fd close failures (`debug`)
- Environment cleanup errors (`warning`, two locations)
- Path stat errors in `get_active_environments_info` (`debug`)
- Orphaned path removal errors (`debug`)
- Execution retry warnings and final failure errors (`warning` / `error`)
- Top-level exception handler in `terminal_tool()` -- this is the only **new** log line (`error`)
- Mini-swe-agent import check (`error`)

### Code Quality Assessment

**Positive:**
- The change is consistent and mechanical -- every error/warning/debug log that catches an exception now includes the traceback.
- CI passes.
- The PR description is thorough and accurate.
- Aligns with the project's `CONTRIBUTING.md` guidance.

**Concerns:**

1. **`exc_info=True` on `logger.debug` calls is noisy for little benefit.** Six of the eleven changes are at `debug` level for routine, expected errors (file stat failures during disk usage scanning, terminal fd cleanup, orphaned path removal). These are "best effort" operations where the exception type and message (already logged) are sufficient. Adding full tracebacks at debug level clutters logs when debug is enabled, without providing meaningful diagnostic value for these trivially understood failures.

2. **`exc_info=True` on `logger.error` for import check is misleading.** The `check_terminal_requirements` call at line 1154 uses `exc_info=True`, but there is no active exception at that point -- `find_spec` returns `None` rather than raising. `exc_info=True` with no active exception just appends `NoneType: None` to the log, which is confusing noise.

3. **The new `logger.error` in the top-level `except Exception as e` block (line 1127) is a welcome addition**, as that handler previously silently swallowed errors into JSON. This is the most valuable part of the PR.

4. **No tests added**, though for a logging-only change this is acceptable.

### Recommendation

**MERGE WITH CHANGES**

The core idea is sound and the most important change (the new `logger.error` in the top-level handler) is clearly valuable. However, two adjustments should be made before merging:

1. **Remove `exc_info=True` from the `logger.error` at line 1154** (mini-swe-agent import check) -- there is no active exception, so `exc_info=True` produces misleading output (`NoneType: None`).
2. **Consider removing `exc_info=True` from the `logger.debug` calls** (6 locations) to avoid excessive noise for routine, expected failures. If the author prefers to keep them, that is acceptable but should be a conscious choice rather than a blanket application.

The `exc_info=True` additions on `logger.warning` and `logger.error` in the retry/failure paths and the new top-level error log are all good and should stay.

   370→+# Copyright (c) 2026 NousResearch / Hermes Agent
   371→+#
   372→+# Matrix platform adapter for the Hermes gateway.
   373→+# Uses mautrix-python for full E2EE + cross-signing support.
   374→+#
   375→+# Dependencies (install via `hermes gateway setup matrix`, or manually):
   376→+#   pip install "mautrix[e2be]" asyncpg aiosqlite base58
   377→+#   System: libolm  (Arch: pacman -S libolm | Debian: apt install libolm-dev)
   378→+#
   379→+# Why asyncpg + aiosqlite?
   380→+#   PgCryptoStore (from mautrix) uses asyncpg's SQL dialect but the aiosqlite
   381→+#   backend lets it run on SQLite without a PostgreSQL server. This stores all
   382→+#   Olm sessions, inbound Megolm sessions, and device keys in a local file so
   383→+#   they survive gateway restarts — the same approach used by maubot and all
   384→+#   production mautrix bridges.
   385→+#
   386→+# Environment variables (configure with `hermes gateway setup matrix`):
   387→+#   MATRIX_HOMESERVER_URL   Required. e.g. https://matrix.example.org
   388→+#   MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN     Required. syt_... bot account access token
   389→+#   MATRIX_USER_ID          Required. @bot:example.org
   390→+#   MATRIX_DEVICE_ID        Recommended. Locks the bot to a specific device so
   391→+#                           E2EE sessions survive restarts without re-verification.
   392→+#   MATRIX_ALLOWED_USERS    Comma-separated user IDs that may message the bot.
   393→+#   MATRIX_HOME_CHANNEL     Optional room ID for cron job delivery.
   394→+#   MATRIX_VERIFY_SSL       true/false (default true; false for self-signed certs)
   395→+#   MATRIX_E2EE             true/false (default false; requires libolm + mautrix[e2be])
   396→+#   MATRIX_[REDACTED]. Bot account password for cross-signing bootstrap.
   397→+#
   398→+# Setup flow:
   399→+#   1. hermes gateway setup matrix   — configure credentials and E2EE
   400→+#   2. hermes gateway run            — start the gateway (uploads device keys)
   401→+#   3. hermes gateway verify-matrix  — establish trust with allowed users (one-time)
   402→+
   403→+from __future__ import annotations
   404→+
   405→+import asyncio
   406→+import logging
   407→+import os
   408→+import re
   409→+import time
   410→+from pathlib import Path

   426→+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   427→+# Python 3.14 compatibility shims for mautrix 0.21.0
   428→+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   429→+
   430→+def _patch_mautrix_py314() -> None:
   431→+    """Monkey-patch mautrix 0.21.0 for Python 3.14 compatibility.
   432→+
   433→+    Python 3.14 tightened several asyncio and stdlib behaviors. This function
   434→+    applies targeted fixes at import time. Most patches are no-ops on Python < 3.14.
   435→+
   436→+    Patches applied:
   437→+    1. MegolmEncryptionMachine._megolm_locks — replace defaultdict(asyncio.Lock)
   438→+       with a plain dict; create locks lazily inside async methods.
   439→+       (Python 3.14: Lock() in defaultdict lambda is created outside a running loop)
   440→+    2. MemoryCryptoStore.transaction() — replace async-def-returning-None with a
   441→+       proper @asynccontextmanager no-op.
   442→+       (Python 3.14: async with None raises TypeError; was silently tolerated before)
   443→+    3. MemoryStateStore.find_shared_rooms() — add missing method that
   444→+       DeviceListMachine calls unconditionally but only asyncpg store implements.
   445→+       (Runtime bug on all Python versions when using MemoryStateStore with device lists)
   446→+    4. MemoryCryptoStore.drop_signatures_by_key() — fix len(None) crash when
   447→+       dict.pop() returns None for a missing key.
   448→+       (mautrix bug present on all Python versions, not version-specific)
   449→+    5. MemoryCryptoStore.put_cross_signing_key() — handle read-only NamedTuple.
   450→+       (Python 3.14: NamedTuple fields became strictly immutable)
   451→+    """
   452→+    import sys
   453→+    import asyncio
   454→+    from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
   455→+
   456→+    # Patch 4 fixes a real mautrix bug present on all Python versions.
   457→+    # Apply it unconditionally so it protects users on Python 3.12/3.13 too.
   458→+    try:
   459→+        from mautrix.crypto.store.memory import MemoryCryptoStore as _MCS_all
   460→+
   461→+        async def _drop_sigs_all(self, signer):
   462→+            deleted = self._signatures.pop(signer, None)
   463→+            return len(deleted) if deleted is not None else 0
   464→+
   465→+        _MCS_all.drop_signatures_by_key = _drop_sigs_all
   466→+    except Exception as e:
   467→+        logger.debug("mautrix patch 4 (drop_signatures_by_key) skipped: %s", e)
   468→+
   469→+    # Patch 3 (find_shared_rooms) is also needed on all Python versions.
   470→+    try:
   471→+        from mautrix.client.state_store import MemoryStateStore as _MSS_all
   472→+
   473→+        if not hasattr(_MSS_all, "find_shared_rooms"):
   474→+            async def _find_shared_rooms_all(self, user_id):
   475→+                return list(getattr(self, "_members", {}).keys())
   476→+
   477→+            _MSS_all.find_shared_rooms = _find_shared_rooms_all
   478→+    except Exception as e:
   479→+        logger.debug("mautrix patch 3 (find_shared_rooms) skipped: %s", e)
   480→+
   481→+    if sys.version_info < (3, 14):
   482→+        return
   483→+
   484→+    # 1. encrypt_megolm: lazy lock creation
   485→+    try:
   486→+        from mautrix.crypto import encrypt_megolm as _emeg
   487→+
   488→+        _orig_emeg_init = _emeg.MegolmEncryptionMachine.__init__
   489→+
   490→+        def _emeg_init(self, *a, **kw):
   491→+            _orig_emeg_init(self, *a, **kw)
   492→+            self._megolm_locks = {}
   493→+
   494→+        _emeg.MegolmEncryptionMachine.__init__ = _emeg_init
   495→+
   496→+        async def _patched_encrypt_meg(self, room_id, event_type, content):
   497→+            if room_id not in self._megolm_locks:
   498→+                self._megolm_locks[room_id] = asyncio.Lock()
   499→+            async with self._megolm_locks[room_id]:
   500→+                return await self._encrypt_megolm_event(room_id, event_type, content)
   501→+
   502→+        _emeg.MegolmEncryptionMachine.encrypt_megolm_event = _patched_encrypt_meg
   503→+    except Exception as e:
   504→+        logger.debug("mautrix py314 patch 1 (encrypt_megolm) skipped: %s", e)
   505→+
   506→+    # 2. MemoryCryptoStore.transaction: proper async context manager
   507→+    try:
   508→+        from mautrix.crypto.store.memory import MemoryCryptoStore as _MCS
   509→+
   510→+        @asynccontextmanager
   511→+        async def _transaction_noop(self):
   512→+            yield
   513→+
   514→+        _MCS.transaction = _transaction_noop
   515→+    except Exception as e:
   516→+        logger.debug("mautrix py314 patch 2 (transaction) skipped: %s", e)
   517→+
   518→+    # 5. MemoryCryptoStore.put_cross_signing_key: handle read-only NamedTuple
   519→+    try:
   520→+        from mautrix.crypto.store.memory import MemoryCryptoStore as _MCS3
   521→+
   522→+        _orig_put_csk = _MCS3.put_cross_signing_key
   523→+
   524→+        async def _put_csk(self, user_id, usage, key):
   525→+            try:
   526→+                await _orig_put_csk(self, user_id, usage, key)
   527→+            except AttributeError:
   528→+                from mautrix.crypto.store.memory import TOFUSigningKey
   529→+                try:
   530→+                    existing = self._cross_signing_keys[user_id][usage]
   531→+                    self._cross_signing_keys[user_id][usage] = TOFUSigningKey(
   532→+                        key=key, first=existing.first
   533→+                    )
   534→+                except (KeyError, TypeError):
   535→+                    self._cross_signing_keys.setdefault(user_id, {})[usage] = (
   536→+                        TOFUSigningKey(key=key, first=key)
   537→+                    )
   538→+
   539→+        _MCS3.put_cross_signing_key = _put_csk
   540→+    except Exception as e:
   541→+        logger.debug("mautrix py314 patch 5 (put_cross_signing_key) skipped: %s", e)
   542→+
   543→+    logger.debug("mautrix Python 3.14 compatibility patches applied")

   586→+
   587→+_MATRIX_ID_RE = re.compile(r"@([^:]{2})[^:]*(:.*)")

   589→+
   590→+def _redact_matrix_id(user_id: str) -> str:
   591→+    """Partially redact a Matrix user ID for safe log output.

   593→+    e.g. ``@alice:example.org`` → ``@al**:example.org``

   608→+
   609→+class MatrixAdapter(BasePlatformAdapter):
   610→+    """Matrix platform adapter backed by mautrix-python.
   611→+
   612→+    Supports both plain-text and fully end-to-end encrypted rooms.
   613→+
   614→+    E2EE design (when MATRIX_E2EE=true):
   615→+    - Uses PgCryptoStore backed by SQLite so all Olm/Megolm sessions survive
   616→+      gateway restarts. This is the same approach used by maubot and all
   617→+      production mautrix bridges.
   618→+    - Cross-signing bootstrap uploads master/self-signing/user-signing keys
   619→+      so Element can display the bot as a verified device.
   620→+    - ``hermes gateway verify-matrix`` signs the bot's master key with each
   621→+      allowed user's identity key, completing the trust chain.
   622→+
   623→+    Non-E2EE design:
   624→+    - Uses the standard mautrix Client without OlmMachine.
   625→+    - Identical message handling, invite acceptance, and media support.
   626→+    """

   637→+        ).rstrip("/")

   639→+        self.access_token: str = (

   641→+        )

   645→+        )

   647→+        # Device ID — pin to a fixed device so E2EE sessions survive restarts.
   648→+        self.device_id: str = (
   649→+            os.getenv("MATRIX_DEVICE_ID") or extra.get("device_id", "")
   650→+        )
   651→+
   652→+        self.allowed_users: set[str] = set(
   653→+            u.strip()
   654→+            for u in (
   655→+                os.getenv("MATRIX_ALLOWED_USERS") or extra.get("allowed_users", "")
   656→+            ).split(",")
   657→+            if u.strip()
   658→+        )
   659→+
   660→+        self.verify_ssl: bool = _bool_env(

   662→+            default=True,
   663→+        )
   664→+
   665→+        self.e2ee: bool = _bool_env(

   687→+        # Resolved at connect time

## PR #1452: fix(cli): silence tirith prefetch install warnings at startup

**Author:** teknium1 | **Status:** Open | **CI:** All checks passing | **Reviews:** None yet

---

### Summary

The PR adds a `log_failures` keyword argument (defaulting to `True`) to three functions in the tirith security scanner module: `ensure_installed()`, `_background_install()`, and `_install_tirith()`. When `log_failures=False` is passed -- as it now is from the CLI and gateway startup prefetch call sites -- warning-level log messages about expected install failures (missing cosign, download failures, etc.) are downgraded to debug-level. This prevents confusing warnings from appearing in the user-facing startup output while preserving the messages for debugging purposes.

### Code Quality Assessment

**Positive:**
- The change is small, focused, and well-scoped (53 additions, 15 deletions across 4 files).
- The approach is clean: a single `log = logger.warning if log_failures else logger.debug` at the top of `_install_tirith` replaces all the individual `logger.warning` calls with `log(...)`, avoiding repetition.
- The default `log_failures=True` preserves existing behavior for all callers other than the two startup prefetch sites.
- Two new test cases are added: one verifying the `kwargs` are threaded through from `ensure_installed` to the background thread, and one verifying that `_install_tirith(log_failures=False)` calls `logger.debug` instead of `logger.warning`.
- The `logger.info` call for "unsupported platform" is intentionally left unchanged, which is correct since that is informational rather than a failure warning.

**Minor observations:**
- The keyword-only argument pattern (`*,`) is used consistently, which is good practice for boolean flags.
- The diff is straightforward with no unrelated changes mixed in.

### Concerns

None of significance. This is a minimal, well-tested fix for a legitimate UX issue. The only thing I would note is that the `_install_tirith` function has one more `logger.warning` call on the checksum verification failure path (line ~350 area) that was *not* converted to use `log(...)`. Looking at the diff, the `_verify_checksum` failure path still uses a direct `logger.warning`. However, that path is arguably a more serious failure (checksum mismatch implies a tampered or corrupted download) where a warning is warranted even during prefetch, so leaving it as-is is a defensible choice.

### Recommendation

**MERGE**

This is a clean, low-risk fix for a real user-facing annoyance. The code is well-structured, the approach is sound, CI is green, and there is adequate test coverage for the new behavior. No blocking issues.

  2001→+## 5. TTS for Mic Breaks
  2002→+
  2003→+For creating radio DJ-style announcements between songs or during station changes. The key requirement is generating natural-sounding speech, saving it to a file (or buffer), and inserting it into the audio playback stream.
  2004→+
  2005→+### Option Comparison
  2006→+
  2007→+| Solution    | Quality    | Cost    | Latency | Offline | Verdict     |
  2008→+|-------------|------------|---------|---------|---------|-------------|
  2009→+| Edge TTS    | High (neural) | Free | ~1-2s   | No      | RECOMMENDED |
  2010→+| ElevenLabs  | Excellent  | $5+/mo  | ~2-4s   | No      | PREMIUM     |
  2011→+| Piper TTS   | Good       | Free    | ~0.5s   | Yes     | FALLBACK    |
  2012→+| say.js      | Low-Med    | Free    | ~0.2s   | Yes     | BASIC       |
  2013→+
  2014→+### Edge TTS (Recommended Default)
  2015→+
  2016→+Uses Microsoft Edge's online neural TTS service. No API key needed, no account required, high-quality neural voices, 400+ voices across 100+ languages. Free with no documented rate limits (uses the same endpoint as Edge browser's Read Aloud feature).
  2017→+
  2018→+#### Best Node.js Packages

  2022→+| `@andresaya/edge-tts` | 1.8.0   | 2025-12     | GPL-3.0 | Most complete API, streaming, word boundaries, 36+ output formats |
  2023→+| `@bestcodes/edge-tts` | 3.0.1   | 2025-12     | MIT     | Clean API, streaming, <50kb bundle, MIT license  |
  2024→+| `node-edge-tts`       | 1.2.10  | 2026-02     | MIT     | Actively maintained, simple promise API, subtitle support |
  2025→+
  2026→+#### Usage with @bestcodes/edge-tts

  2048→+// Stream chunks for real-time playback

  2051→+}

  2138→+### say.js (System TTS Fallback)
  2139→+
  2140→+Uses platform-native TTS: macOS `say`, Windows SAPI, Linux Festival. Quality varies by platform -- macOS has decent neural voices, Linux Festival sounds robotic. Good as a zero-dependency fallback.
  2141→+
